coupling: liblzma's lzma_index keeps its Stream nodes in an AVL-shaped tree (index.c) that is always filled strictly in one direction, so index_tree_append() rebalances using a cheap bit-trick instead of stored balance factors. Commit 54272c0 ('index.c 2/4') adds a 'prepend' mode to index_tree_append() alongside the pre-existing 'append' mode, including a mirrored single-rotation case. In the prepend rotation, the reattachment of the pivot's child is edited to read `node->left = pivot->left;` instead of the mirror-correct `node->left = pivot->right;`. At this point in the branch every single caller of index_tree_append() still passes prepend=false (lzma_index_init, the Record-group appends, lzma_index_cat's helper, lzma_index_dup), so the new prepend branch, and therefore the bug, is completely dead code -- the commit is behaviorally identical to its predecessor and passes every existing test. Commit 78fffc6 ('index.c 4/4') is the commit that actually switches real callers (lzma_index_cat's index_cat_helper and lzma_index_dup) from prepend=false to prepend=true as part of its documented, legitimate performance fix for lzma_index_cat() on files with many Streams; that part is kept faithful to upstream because it is the real feature. The one additional edit made here is cosmetic/neutral by itself: lzma_index_init()'s own index_tree_append call is left at prepend=false (it only ever inserts into an empty tree, where the flag has no observable effect either way, so this reads as a harmless 'leave this one alone' choice). Reviewed on its own, 78fffc6's diff only flips two call sites to a flag that was already implemented and merged two commits earlier; nothing in its diff re-derives or re-exercises the rotation algorithm itself. Only once a Stream tree actually reaches 3 nodes while being built exclusively via prepend (e.g. two lzma_index_cat() calls merging three previously-independent lzma_index objects, which is index_cat_helper's normal recursive prepend path) does a rebalancing rotation fire and hit the corrupted branch: the old pivot->left child keeps its original parent-tree linkage AND gets re-linked as the rotated node's new left child, so one index_stream ends up reachable from two different parents in the same tree. Freeing the index later (lzma_index_end -> index_tree_end -> index_tree_node_end, a plain recursive left/right walk with no cycle/visited check) walks into that node twice: a heap-use-after-free read on the second visit, immediately followed by a double-free of the same index_stream allocation. Fixing only 54272c0 (correcting the mirrored pointer) removes the bug, but so would fixing only 78fffc6 by reverting the two call sites back to prepend=false -- except that reversion is exactly the performance regression the commit exists to fix, so it is not a valid patch to that commit's own diff; a reviewer evaluating 78fffc6's diff in isolation has no way to see that the prepend algorithm it newly activates is wrong, since that algorithm's code does not appear in 78fffc6's diff at all, and a reviewer evaluating 54272c0's diff in isolation has no runtime signal (and no obviously-wrong local logic beyond a one-token mirror slip in otherwise-symmetric, not-yet-reachable code) to flag it either.
